items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: So what happened was, we started to play together with a jazz band. We didn't have a name for the band. And me being the cornet player, I was the leader.

ctx.x: Well I haven't mentioned it to you yet, but my father was a professional boxer, a professional musician and a professional baseball player. So he taught my brother and I since we were kids, since we were five years old we both started to learn how to play the violin. And also to learn to box, and to play baseball.

So we got to be good athletes you know. Good boxers, we could handle ourselves in any street fights or gangs like we used to have in those days on the west side of Chicago. And we could box and we could hit pretty hard. So what happened was, we started to play together with a jazz band. We didn't have a name for the band. And me being the cornet player, I was the leader. And I was almost like the leader of the gang because in crowds when any trouble would start why my brother would say, okay Cocky, you want to…
I take it that was your family nickname?
